newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares reverse early gains, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares reverse early gains, end lower.

text.p: Manila shares skidded at the close on Friday as a strong opening prompted investors to take profits on select first and secondliner issues late in the session, traders said.

"A lot of people are confused as to where the market will go. There's still the question on capabilities of companies considering disappoining first quarter earnings," said Dennis Rayala, research head at Abacus Securities Corp.
The main index closed way off its intra-day high of 2,707.41 points. But week-on-week, the market's barometer gained 65.74 points, a 2.52 percent rise, from the previous week's 2,605.65.
A fresh wave of selling hit cellular phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp on news that brokers had downgraded their earnings forecast for the company.
The issue reached a record low of 8.70 but was able to recover, closing 20 centavos higher at 10 pesos.

"I expect that disappointing corporate results have caused sentiment to further deteriorate. Hardly anybody is doing anything but since there's still negative news on first quarter earnings, this egged on selling," said Juan Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities Philippines Inc.
Among blue chips, Manila Electric Corp B led the wave of selling closing nine pesos lower at 120 pesos.
Diversified Securities Inc executive vice-president Jose Ricardo Garcia said the market will likely trade in a narrow range next week.
The Philippine Stock Exchange said there will be no trading on May 12 declared a holiday due to local elections.
